The `SSLHandshakeException: Trust anchor for certification path not found` occurred because the dev server uses a custom self-signed CA certificate (`dev-ca/shelftap-dev-ca.pem`), which Android does not trust by default.

To fix this securely without compromising production/release traffic:

1. **Added the dev CA certificate to Android resources:**
   - Placed the certificate at [shelftap_dev_ca.pem](file:///mnt/01DC198BE9192500/github/Schooldev/3S-study-work/trials/e4/c2-agy-B-r4/work/app/src/main/res/raw/shelftap_dev_ca.pem).

2. **Configured Network Security Config with `debug-overrides`:**
   - Created [network_security_config.xml](file:///mnt/01DC198BE9192500/github/Schooldev/3S-study-work/trials/e4/c2-agy-B-r4/work/app/src/main/res/xml/network_security_config.xml) trusting `@raw/shelftap_dev_ca` inside `<debug-overrides>`. This ensures the custom CA is trusted only in debug builds (`android:debuggable="true"`), while release builds remain strictly protected using the system trust store.

3. **Applied the configuration in the manifest:**
   - Updated [AndroidManifest.xml](file:///mnt/01DC198BE9192500/github/Schooldev/3S-study-work/trials/e4/c2-agy-B-r4/work/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml#L8) to reference `android:networkSecurityConfig="@xml/network_security_config"` on the `<application>` tag.
